Let $x$ be an $n$-dimensional state vector, $u$ an $m$-dimensional control vector, $A$ an $n$ by $n$ matrix, and $B$ an $n$ by $m$ matrix.
\[\dot{x}=Ax+Bu\]

In a continuous state-space model, $z\in\mathbb R^p$, $v\in\mathbb R^r$, $F\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, and $G\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}$.
$\dot{z} = Fz + Gv$.

Let $q$ denote the $d$-dimensional state and $w$ the $c$-dimensional input. Let $M$ and $N$ be $d$ by $d$ and $d$ by $c$ matrices, respectively.

$$\dot{q}=Mq+Nw$$

The vectors $s\in\mathbb R^n$ and $r\in\mathbb R^m$ are the state and control input. The matrices satisfy $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $L\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[Ks+Lr=\dot{s}\]

Let $y$ be an $a$-vector and $e$ a $b$-vector. Let $C$ be $a$ by $a$ and $D$ be $a$ by $b$.
\[\dot{y}=(Cy)+(De)\]

For the control system, $\xi$ is an $n$-dimensional state vector, $\eta$ is an $m$-dimensional control input, $H$ is $n\times n$, and $J$ is $n\times m$.
$\dot{\xi}=H\xi+J\eta$.

Let $p\in\mathbb R^k$ and $c\in\mathbb R^j$. The state and input matrices are $R\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$ and $S\in\mathbb R^{k\times j}$.
\[\dot{p}=Rp+Sc\]

The bold symbols $\mathbf X\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbf U\in\mathbb R^m$ are vectors; $\mathbf F\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $\mathbf G\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ are matrices.
\[\dot{\mathbf X}=\mathbf F\mathbf X+\mathbf G\mathbf U\]

Let $\chi\in\mathbb R^n$, $\nu\in\mathbb R^m$, $K_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $L_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{\chi}=K_0\chi+L_0\nu\]

In continuous time, $\zeta$ is a state in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mu$ is an input in $\mathbb R^m$. Matrices $A_c$ and $B_c$ have sizes $n\times n$ and $n\times m$.
\[\frac{d\zeta}{dt}=A_c\zeta+B_c\mu\]

The state $h$ and input $j$ have dimensions $n$ and $m$. Let $A_1$ be $n$ by $n$ and $B_1$ be $n$ by $m$.
\[A_1h+B_1j=\dot{h}\]

Let $s_1\in\mathbb R^d$, $v_1\in\mathbb R^c$, $K_1\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, and $L_1\in\mathbb R^{d\times c}$.
\[\dot{s_1}=\left(K_1s_1\right)+\left(L_1v_1\right)\]

Take $\omega\in\mathbb R^n$ as the state and $\tau\in\mathbb R^m$ as the control. Here $E\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $F\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
$\frac{d}{dt}\omega=E\omega+F\tau$.

Let $a\in\mathbb R^n$, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, $F_a\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $G_a\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\begin{align}\dot{a}&=F_a a+G_a b\end{align}

The vectors $\rho\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\sigma\in\mathbb R^m$ are state and input; $U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $V\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ are their system matrices.
\begin{equation}\dot{\rho} = U\rho + V\sigma\end{equation}

Let $x_s$ and $u_s$ denote an $n$-dimensional state vector and an $m$-dimensional control vector, respectively. Let $A_s$ and $B_s$ denote an $n$ by $n$ state matrix and an $n$ by $m$ input matrix, respectively.
\[\dot{x_s}=A_sx_s+B_su_s\]

The model is
\[\dot{x_f}=A_fx_f+B_fu_f\]
where $x_f\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_f\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_f\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_f\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
A realization obeys $\dot{q_c}=M_cq_c+N_cw_c$. Here $q_c$ is an $r$-vector, $w_c$ is an $s$-vector, $M_c$ is $r$ by $r$, and $N_c$ is $r$ by $s$.

\input{dims21}
The continuous model is \[\dot{x_{21}}=A_{21}x_{21}+B_{21}u_{21}\]
Let $x_{21}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{21}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{21}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{21}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.

Let $z_{22}\in\mathbb R^p$, $v_{22}\in\mathbb R^r$, $F_{22}\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, and $G_{22}\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}$.
\input{model22}

The plant dynamics are
\[\dot{z_{22}}=F_{22}z_{22}+G_{22}v_{22}\]

\input{defs23}
\input{dynamics23}
Let $q_{23}$ and $w_{23}$ be vectors of dimensions $d$ and $c$. Let $M_{23}$ and $N_{23}$ have sizes $d\times d$ and $d\times c$.
\begin{equation}\dot{q_{23}}=M_{23}q_{23}+N_{23}w_{23}\end{equation}

# Plant model

The state $s_{24}\in\mathbb R^n$, input $r_{24}\in\mathbb R^m$, and matrices $K_{24}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $L_{24}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ satisfy

$$\dot{s_{24}}=K_{24}s_{24}+L_{24}r_{24}$$

Let $y_{25}\in\mathbb R^a$, $e_{25}\in\mathbb R^b$, $C_{25}\in\mathbb R^{a\times a}$, and $D_{25}\in\mathbb R^{a\times b}$.
\[\displaystyle \dot{y_{25}}=C_{25}y_{25}+D_{25}e_{25}\]

Let $p_{26}$ be an $n$-state, $c_{26}$ an $m$-input, $R_{26}$ an $n\times n$ matrix, and $S_{26}$ an $n\times m$ matrix.
\[\dot{p_{26}}=\bigl(R_{26}p_{26}\bigr)+\bigl(S_{26}c_{26}\bigr)\]

The declarations $x_r\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_r\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_r\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_r\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ apply throughout.
\[\dot{x_r} = A_r {x_r}+B_r {u_r}\]

Let $z_r\in\mathbb R^p$, $v_r\in\mathbb R^r$, $F_r\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, and $G_r\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}$.
\[\left(F_rz_r+G_rv_r\right)=\dot{z_r}\]

The state-space vectors are $\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\boldsymbol{u}\in\mathbb R^m$; its matrices are $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $\boldsymbol{B}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{\boldsymbol{x}}=\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{B}\boldsymbol{u}\]

Let $\theta\in\mathbb R^n$ be the state and $\upsilon\in\mathbb R^m$ the input. Let $\mathcal F\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $\mathcal G\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{\theta}=\mathcal F\theta+\mathcal G\upsilon\]

Let $x_{31}$ be a scalar, $u_{31}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{31}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{31}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{31}}=A_{31}x_{31}+B_{31}u_{31}\]

Let $x_{32}\in\mathbb R^n$ and $u_{32}\in\mathbb R^m$. Let $A_{32}$ be an $n$-dimensional vector and $B_{32}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{32}}=A_{32}x_{32}+B_{32}u_{32}\]

Let $n\ne m$. Let $x_{33}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{33}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{33}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{33}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[\dot{x_{33}}=A_{33}x_{33}+B_{33}u_{33}\]

Let $n\ne p$, $x_{34}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{34}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{34}\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, and $B_{34}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{34}}=A_{34}x_{34}+B_{34}u_{34}\]

Let $n\ne p$, $x_{35}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{35}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{35}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{35}\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{35}}=A_{35}x_{35}+B_{35}u_{35}\]

Let $x_{36}$ and $y_{36}$ be distinct $n$-dimensional states, $u_{36}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{36}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{36}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{y_{36}}=A_{36}x_{36}+B_{36}u_{36}\]

Let $x_{37}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{37}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{37}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{37}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[x_{37}=A_{37}x_{37}+B_{37}u_{37}\]

Let $x_{38}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{38}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{38}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{38}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\ddot{x_{38}}=A_{38}x_{38}+B_{38}u_{38}\]

Let $x_k\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_k\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_d\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_d\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[x_{k+1}=A_dx_k+B_du_k\]

Let $x_{40},u_{40}$ be compatible vectors and $A_{40},B_{40}$ compatible matrices. Here $\odot$ is elementwise multiplication.
\[\dot{x_{40}}=A_{40}\odot x_{40}+B_{40}\odot u_{40}\]

Let $x_{41}\in\mathbb R^n$ and use column-vector convention. Let $A_{41}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $B_{41}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$, and $u_{41}\in\mathbb R^m$.
\[\dot{x_{41}}=x_{41}A_{41}+B_{41}u_{41}\]

Let $x_{42}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{42}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{42}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{42}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{42}}=A_{42}x_{42}+B_{42}(u_{42})^2\]

Let $x_{43}$ and $u_{43}$ be vectors in $\mathbb R^n$ and let $A_{43}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[\dot{x_{43}}=A_{43}x_{43}+u_{43}\]

Let $x_{44}\in\mathbb R^n$. Let $u_{44}\in\mathbb R^m$ and $v_{44}\in\mathbb R^r$ be independent controls, with $B_{44}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ and $C_{44}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$; let $A_{44}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[\dot{x_{44}}=A_{44}x_{44}+B_{44}u_{44}+C_{44}v_{44}\]

Let $x_{45}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{45}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{45}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{45}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{45}}\le A_{45}x_{45}+B_{45}u_{45}\]

A control system uses symbols $x_{46},u_{46},A_{46},B_{46}$, with no shape declarations.
\[\dot{x_{46}}=A_{46}x_{46}+B_{46}u_{46}\]

The standalone equation is
\[\dot{x_{47}}=A_{47}x_{47}+B_{47}u_{47}\]
Let $x_{47}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{47}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{47}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{47}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.

Let $x_{48}$ be an $n$-dimensional vector. In the same scope, let $x_{48}$ be a scalar. Let $u_{48}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{48}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{48}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{48}}=A_{48}x_{48}+B_{48}u_{48}\]

Let $n\ne p$. Let $x_{50}\in\mathbb R^n$, $u_{50}\in\mathbb R^m$, $A_{50}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $B_{50}\in\mathbb R^{p\times m}$.
\[\dot{x_{50}}=(A_{50}x_{50})+(B_{50}u_{50})\]

Let $A$, $P$, and $Q$ be real $n$ by $n$ matrices.
\[A^TP+PA=-Q\]

For a continuous-time system, $F,X,R\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$.
\[F^\top X+XF=-R\]

Let $M$ be the system matrix, $H$ the Lyapunov certificate, and $S$ the forcing matrix; all are $d$ by $d$.

$$M^{T}H+HM=-S$$

Let $K,Y,W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$. The continuous Lyapunov relation is
\[-W=K^{\top}Y+YK\]

The matrices $L,Z,N$ are square with common order $r$.
\[ZL+L^TZ=-N\]

Let $C$, $P_c$, and $Q_c$ be $n\times n$ matrices.
\[\left(C^\top P_c\right)+\left(P_cC\right)=-Q_c\]

Let $D$, $X_d$, and $R_d$ be square matrices of size $m$.
\begin{align}D^\top X_d+X_dD&=-R_d\end{align}

Matrices $E,H_e,S_e\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$ are fixed.
\[E^{\mathsf T}H_e+H_eE=-S_e\]

Let $F_i$, $P_i$, and $Q_i$ be real square matrices with the same dimension.
\[F_i^{\intercal}P_i+P_iF_i=-Q_i\]

Under real-matrix convention, the prime denotes transpose. Let $G,J,T$ be $n$ by $n$ matrices.
\[G'J+JG=-T\]

Let $A_c,P_c,W_c\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[A_c^TP_c+P_cA_c=-(W_c)\]

Let $B,L_b,N_b$ be square matrices of common dimension.
\[0=B^TL_b+L_bB+N_b\]

The matrices $C,Y_c,Q_y$ are all $r\times r$.
\[C^\top Y_c+Y_cC+Q_y=0\]

Let $D,Z_d,R_z\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$.
\[R_z=-\bigl(D^TZ_d+Z_dD\bigr)\]

Let $E$, $H$, and $S$ denote the state matrix, Lyapunov matrix, and forcing matrix, respectively; each is $n$ by $n$.
\[E^TH+HE=-S\]

The certificate equation is
\[F_{16}^\top P_{16}+P_{16}F_{16}=-Q_{16}\]
where $F_{16},P_{16},Q_{16}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
A stability calculation uses $-R_{17}=G_{17}^TX_{17}+X_{17}G_{17}$. Here $G_{17}$, $X_{17}$, and $R_{17}$ are square matrices of order $p$.
Let $A_{20}$, $P_{20}$, and $Q_{20}$ be $n$ by $n$ matrices.

Let $F_{21},X_{21},R_{21}\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$.
\input{certificate21}

The Lyapunov identity is
\[F_{21}^\top X_{21}+X_{21}F_{21}=-R_{21}\]

\input{square22}
\input{relation22}
The matrices $M_{22}$, $H_{22}$, and $S_{22}$ are square with common order $d$.
\begin{equation}M_{22}^{\mathsf T}H_{22}+H_{22}M_{22}=-S_{22}\end{equation}

# Stability certificate

Let $K_{23},Y_{23},W_{23}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.

$$K_{23}^{\top}Y_{23}+Y_{23}K_{23}=-W_{23}$$

Let $L_{24},Z_{24},N_{24}$ be real square matrices of the same size.
\[\left(L_{24}^\top Z_{24}\right)+\left(Z_{24}L_{24}\right)=-N_{24}\]

The calligraphic matrices $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal P$, and $\mathcal Q$ lie in $\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[\mathcal A^{\top}\mathcal P+\mathcal P\mathcal A=-\mathcal Q\]

Let $\mathbf A,\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$.
\[\mathbf A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf P+\mathbf P\mathbf A=-\mathbf Q\]

cursor.needle: \mathbf A^{\mathsf T}\mathbf P+\mathbf P\mathbf A=-\mathbf Q

Matrices $F_r$, $X_r$, and $R_r$ are all $p$ by $p$.
\[F_r ^ {\top} X_r + X_r F_r = - R_r\]

Let $M_a,H_a,S_a\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$.
\[\begin{aligned}M_a^T H_a&+H_aM_a\\&=-S_a\end{aligned}\]

Let $K_b,Y_b,\Omega_b$ be square matrices with common order $n$.
\[-\Omega_b=\bigl(K_b^{\intercal}Y_b\bigr)+\bigl(Y_bK_b\bigr)\]

Let $n\ne m$, $A_{31}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $P_{31}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$, and $Q_{31}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[A_{31}^TP_{31}+P_{31}A_{31}=-Q_{31}\]

Let $n\ne m$, $A_{32}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $P_{32}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$, and $Q_{32}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.
\[A_{32}^TP_{32}+P_{32}A_{32}=-Q_{32}\]

Let $n\ne m$, $A_{33},P_{33}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $Q_{33}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$.
\[A_{33}^{\top}P_{33}+P_{33}A_{33}=-Q_{33}\]

Let $A_{39},P_{39},Q_{39}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $B_{39}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$, and invertible $R_{39}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$.
\[A_{39}^TP_{39}+P_{39}A_{39}-P_{39}B_{39}R_{39}^{-1}B_{39}^TP_{39}=-Q_{39}\]

Let $A_{41},P_{41},Q_{41}$ be same-sized square matrices, and let $\odot$ denote entrywise multiplication.
\[A_{41}^T\odot P_{41}+P_{41}\odot A_{41}=-Q_{41}\]

Let $A_{44},P_{44}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and let $q_{44}\in\mathbb R^n$ be a forcing vector.
\[A_{44}^TP_{44}+P_{44}A_{44}=-q_{44}\]

A stability discussion introduces $A_{45}$, $P_{45}$, and $Q_{45}$ without declaring their shapes.
\[A_{45}^TP_{45}+P_{45}A_{45}=-Q_{45}\]

The isolated relation is
\[A_{46}^TP_{46}+P_{46}A_{46}=-Q_{46}\]
Let $A_{46},P_{46},Q_{46}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$.

Let $A_{47},P_{47},Q_{47}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$. In the same scope, let $P_{47}$ be an $n$-dimensional vector.
\[A_{47}^TP_{47}+P_{47}A_{47}=-Q_{47}\]

Let $A_{48},P_{48},Q_{48}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$; no matrix $R_{48}$ is declared.
\[A_{48}^TP_{48}+P_{48}A_{48}=-R_{48}\]

Let $n\ne m$ and let $A_{50},P_{50},Q_{50}\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ be rectangular matrices.
\[A_{50}^TP_{50}+P_{50}A_{50}=-Q_{50}\]
